titleStmt.title: Neural correlates of learning and working memory in the primate posterior parietal cortex
titleStmt.author: Rawley
Constantinidis

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Neural correlates of learning and working memory in the primate posterior parietal cortex

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: what the primate posterior parietal cortex contributes to working memory and to learning, against a tradition that assigned both to prefrontal cortex
span.quote: Working memory has traditionally been ascribed to the prefrontal cortex (PFC), but a wealth of recent research demonstrates that posterior parietal cortex is not only activated during working memory, but that inactivation of, or damage to posterior parietal regions can cause specific working memory deficits.

span.label: whether parietal activity during memory and after training is a distinct contribution or a copy of the prefrontal signal
span.quote: During working memory, posterior parietal neurons continue to discharge and to represent stimuli that are no longer present. This activation resembles the responses of prefrontal neurons, although important differences have been identified in terms of the ability to resist stimulation by distracting stimuli, which is more evident in the prefrontal than the posterior parietal cortex.

span.label: collects the evidence that parietal neurons hold stimuli after they vanish and are reshaped by training, and identifies distractor resistance as the property that separates parietal from prefrontal memory activity
span.quote: During working memory, posterior parietal neurons continue to discharge and to represent stimuli that are no longer present. This activation resembles the responses of prefrontal neurons, although important differences have been identified in terms of the ability to resist stimulation by distracting stimuli, which is more evident in the prefrontal than the posterior parietal cortex.

span.label: existence
span.quote: These findings demonstrate the importance of posterior parietal cortex in brain networks mediating working memory and learning.

span.label: working memory and learning in posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: More recently, involvement of posterior parietal cortex in other cognitive functions such as working memory and task learning has become evident.

span.label: review
span.quote: We will provide a brief overview of these functions next, and focus on the latter two for the remainder of this review.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Delay-period activity is sustained because reciprocally connected pyramidal neurons re-excite each other, so discharges keep reverberating around the recurrent circuit after the stimulus is gone.
span.quote: Reverberating activity within recurrent circuits is a characteristic of this type of architecture: pyramidal neurons form reciprocal, excitatory connections between them and transmit action potentials to each other so that, even when the original stimulus is no longer present, discharges continue to reverberate in the network.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Slow postsynaptic receptors (NMDA) keep the postsynaptic cell excited long enough for sparse presynaptic inputs to accumulate, which is what allows low-firing-rate cortical neurons to sustain reverberation.
span.quote: Given the fairly low firing rate of cortical pyramidal neurons, postsynaptic receptors with fairly slow time constants are essential for this function.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Damage to spatial working memory nodes destroys the record of which locations have already been searched, and that failure of book-keeping in the good hemifield compounds the failure to attend to the contralesional one.
span.quote: These studies support the idea that when important nodes in the spatial working memory network are compromised or deafferented, an inability to keep track of previously searched locations in the ipsilateral hemifield may contribute to the failure to attend to the contralateral one ( Driver, 2002 ; Malhotra, 2005 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Parietal episodic-memory deficits arise because bottom-up processes no longer capture attention toward internally stored memories, so unprompted recall misses details that a top-down cue can still retrieve.
span.quote: Episodic memory deficits described in free recall tasks may be attributed to a failure of bottom up processes to capture attention, a phenomenon termed “memory neglect” ( Cabeza, 2008 ; Cabeza, Ciaramelli, Olson, & Moscovitch, 2008 ).

span.label: sustained activity is modelled as reverberation in recurrent excitatory loops that keeps firing after the stimulus is gone
span.quote: Reverberating activity within recurrent circuits is a characteristic of this type of architecture: pyramidal neurons form reciprocal, excitatory connections between them and transmit action potentials to each other so that, even when the original stimulus is no longer present, discharges continue to reverberate in the network.

span.label: the slow NMDA receptor is proposed as the element that lets sparse pyramidal firing sustain itself
span.quote: A critical property revealed by models is that discharges can be sustained if the postsynaptic neuron continues to be in an excited state at the time presynaptic inputs accumulate. Given the fairly low firing rate of cortical pyramidal neurons, postsynaptic receptors with fairly slow time constants are essential for this function. The NMDA receptor has therefore been proposed as a critical element of cortical circuits involved in working memory

span.label: such networks settle into attractor states, with or without oscillation depending on the instantiation
span.quote: Reverberatory networks, when left unperturbed, will settle into an attractor state defined by a stereotyped pattern of activity within the network ( Hopfield, 1982 ). Attractor models may undergo spontaneous oscillations, although network instantiations have also been shown to be capable of mediating sustained responses without oscillatory discharges

span.label: spiking may not be the only carrier - intracellular and synaptic mechanisms are left open
span.quote: These models emphasize the importance of spiking mechanisms as a means for the maintenance of working memory, however it is possible that intracellular and synaptic mechanisms may also play a role

span.label: training changes what parietal neurons are selective for: colour selectivity appears when colour becomes task-relevant
span.quote: PPC neurons typically have low selectivity for color; only a small percentage of area 7a neurons demonstrate significantly different responses to green and red stimuli of equal luminance ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 2001 ). However when animals execute a behavioral task for which color is important because it signifies eye movements, a larger percentage of PPC neurons exhibit selectivity for the color of the stimuli

span.label: The review's physiological coverage is restricted to areas LIP and 7a rather than the whole of posterior parietal cortex.
span.quote: The bulk of physiological studies related to working memory have been conducted in areas LIP and 7a and these will be the basis of our review.

span.label: The evidence base lacks direct multi-area comparisons in monkeys, so functional differences between parietal areas are not firmly established.
span.quote: However, few monkey neurophysiological studies have directly compared neuronal responses in multiple cortical areas in order to establish clear functional differences between them.

span.label: The monkey-to-human mapping of parietal subdivisions that the review relies on is unresolved.
span.quote: Therefore, the functional correspondence between monkey and human areas remains unclear.

span.label: the correspondence between monkey and human parietal areas remains unclear, because few studies compare several areas directly
span.quote: However, few monkey neurophysiological studies have directly compared neuronal responses in multiple cortical areas in order to establish clear functional differences between them. Therefore, the functional correspondence between monkey and human areas remains unclear.

span.label: competing naming schemes and areas present in one species' atlas but not the other have impeded functional correspondence
span.quote: This anatomical ambiguity has impeded the establishment of a functional correspondence between human and monkey parietal areas, though some insights have been gained recently.

span.label: the boundary of the region itself is defined loosely, by sulci
span.quote: One can loosely define the boundary delineated by the Sylvian Sulcus (SS), the Superior Temporal Sulcus (STS) and the bend in the Lunate Sulcus, as the posterior-lateral edge of the PPC

span.label: the psychological subsystems of working memory are functional units and should not be read as brain regions
span.quote: It should be made clear however that these working memory subsystems refer to functional rather than anatomical units ( Constantinidis & Procyk, 2004 ; Goldman-Rakic, 1995 ). For example, the prefrontal cortex seems a logical functional neural analogue to the central executive. However, physiological evidence indicates that prefrontal neurons in area 46 represent spatial and object attributes of visual memoranda in correspondence to the visual-spatial sketchpad ( Rao, Rainer, & Miller, 1997 ) while at the same time they provide neural correlates of executive functions such as rule execution and category classification

span.label: the text is an accepted manuscript before copyediting, and the publisher warns errors may remain
span.note: retracted: A LIMITATION TAG WHOSE QUOTE IS THE PUBLISHER'S PROOF NOTICE. The evidence is: 'THIS IS A PDF FILE OF AN UNEDITED MANUSCRIPT that has been accepted for publication. AS A SERVICE TO OUR CUSTOMERS we are providing this early version of the manuscript. The manuscript will undergo co[pyediting]...' That is boilerplate printed on every article-in-press this publisher issues. The manuscript will undergo copyediting, typesetting, and review of the resulting proof before it is published in its final citable form. span.label: Baddeley's four-subsystem model of working memory, imported as the framework for describing what is held and manipulated
span.quote: Recent models propose four subsystems of working memory, a “central executive,” responsible for controlling and coordinating information through “slave” systems called the visual-spatial sketchpad for manipulation of visual objects, the phonological loop for verbal rehearsal, and the latest addition, an episodic buffer, that allows for temporal storage and binding of information within the other subsidiary subsystems

span.label: attractor dynamics, used to describe how a recurrent network holds a state
span.quote: Reverberatory networks, when left unperturbed, will settle into an attractor state defined by a stereotyped pattern of activity within the network ( Hopfield, 1982 ). Attractor models may undergo spontaneous oscillations, although network instantiations have also been shown to be capable of mediating sustained responses without oscillatory discharges

span.label: the neglect syndrome, the signature deficit after parietal damage and the original evidence for parietal function
span.quote: Perhaps the signature effect of PPC damage is the neglect syndrome, typically occurring after a lesion in the right hemisphere. Disturbances include the inability to detect an object in the contralateral (left) visual hemifield (egocentric neglect) or to perceive the left side of objects, regardless of where they appear within the visual field (allocentric neglect).

span.label: working memory and short-term memory name the SAME system; the newer term marks an emphasis on manipulation rather than storage, not a different referent
span.quote: Working memory does not refer to a memory system that differs from that of short-term memory; the term rather emphasizes that this type of memory does not function simply as a passive storage of information but it allows integration of remembered information with current contingencies and future goals.

span.label: posterior parietal cortex has no single delineation: Brodmann, von Economo-Koskinas and von Bonin-Bailey each name the same tissue differently, and areas 39 and 40 exist in the human scheme but not the monkey one
span.quote: The gross level differences in area placements between species are immediately obvious in the anatomical atlases. In the human, Brodmann’s areas 5 and 7 reside within the superior temporal lobule while areas 40 and 39 occupy most of the inferior parietal lobule. In monkeys, area 5 is found in the superior parietal lobule whereas areas 7a and 7b fall in the inferior parietal lobule. Brodmann’s Areas 39 and 40 have not been identified in the monkey.

span.label: central executive, visual-spatial sketchpad and phonological loop are FUNCTIONAL units of a psychological model, explicitly not anatomical ones
span.quote: It should be made clear however that these working memory subsystems refer to functional rather than anatomical units ( Constantinidis & Procyk, 2004 ; Goldman-Rakic, 1995 ). For example, the prefrontal cortex seems a logical functional neural analogue to the central executive. However, physiological evidence indicates that prefrontal neurons in area 46 represent spatial and object attributes of visual memoranda in correspondence to the visual-spatial sketchpad ( Rao, Rainer, & Miller, 1997 ) while at the same time they provide neural correlates of executive functions such as rule execution and category classification

span.label: egocentric and allocentric are two frames of reference, the second phylogenetically recent and late-developing in humans
span.quote: These coordinate subsystems are encompassed by two larger points of view within the world schema: that of the egocentric observer, who understands the disposition of surrounding space and its contents in relationship to itself, and that of the allocentric point of view in which spatial maps are constructed based upon landmarks or relationships of objects relative to one another

span.label: this record is a REVIEW - every finding in it is another paper's, and the quotes are the reviewers' summary rather than a primary report
span.quote: Functions of the PPC can be grouped in four domains: sensorimotor transformations, selective attention, working memory, and learning. We will provide a brief overview of these functions next, and focus on the latter two for the remainder of this review.

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: existence — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: The posterior parietal cortex has been traditionally associated with coordinate transformations necessary for interaction with the environment and with visual-spatial attention. More recently, involvement of posterior parietal cortex in other cognitive functions such as working memory and task learning has become evident.

span.label: method: narrative review of monkey single-unit recording, human imaging, lesion and stimulation studies; no new data
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: review — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Functions of the PPC can be grouped in four domains: sensorimotor transformations, selective attention, working memory, and learning. We will provide a brief overview of these functions next, and focus on the latter two for the remainder of this review.

span.label: phenomenon: sustained neuronal discharge representing a stimulus that is no longer present
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: working memory and learning in posterior parietal cortex — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: During working memory, posterior parietal neurons continue to discharge and to represent stimuli that are no longer present. This activation resembles the responses of prefrontal neurons, although important differences have been identified in terms of the ability to resist stimulation by distracting stimuli, which is more evident in the prefrontal than the posterior parietal cortex.

span.label: qualifies → the tradition assigning working memory to prefrontal cortex alone
span.quote: Working memory has traditionally been ascribed to the prefrontal cortex (PFC), but a wealth of recent research demonstrates that posterior parietal cortex is not only activated during working memory, but that inactivation of, or damage to posterior parietal regions can cause specific working memory deficits.

span.label: critiques → attempts to map Baddeley's working memory subsystems onto brain regions
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS FUNCTIONAL VERSUS ANATOMICAL INDIVIDUATION. 'these working memory subsystems REFER TO FUNCTIONAL RATHER THAN ANATOMICAL UNITS ... For example, the prefrontal cortex seems a logical functional neural analogue to the central executive. However, physiological evidence indicates that prefrontal neurons in area 46 represent spatial and ob[ject information].' The mapping from a model component to a brain region is denied as an identity while kept as an analogy. Q-448.
span.quote: It should be made clear however that these working memory subsystems refer to functional rather than anatomical units ( Constantinidis & Procyk, 2004 ; Goldman-Rakic, 1995 ). For example, the prefrontal cortex seems a logical functional neural analogue to the central executive. However, physiological evidence indicates that prefrontal neurons in area 46 represent spatial and object attributes of visual memoranda in correspondence to the visual-spatial sketchpad ( Rao, Rainer, & Miller, 1997 ) while at the same time they provide neural correlates of executive functions such as rule execution and category classification

span.label: critiques → the cross-species area nomenclature inherited from the pioneering anatomists
span.quote: A source of confusion regarding PPC organization and function involves the correspondence between human and monkey PPC subdivisions. The first part of this dilemma arises from the discrepancy of area assignments from one species to another and the various naming schemes that have been applied by the pioneering anatomists.

span.label: supports → reverberatory recurrent-network accounts of sustained delay activity
span.quote: Reverberating activity within recurrent circuits is a characteristic of this type of architecture: pyramidal neurons form reciprocal, excitatory connections between them and transmit action potentials to each other so that, even when the original stimulus is no longer present, discharges continue to reverberate in the network.

span.label: reconciles → prefrontal and parietal accounts of delay activity, by assigning them different roles in one network
span.quote: These results suggest that posterior parietal cortex encodes the memory of the last stimulus location whereas prefrontal areas are critical for mental operations that span multiple items of a sequence of stimuli.

span.label: posterior parietal cortex —distinct-from→ prefrontal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: parietal memory activity is overwritten by an intervening distractor and prefrontal activity is not. The two are indistinguishable on the usual measure - see the identical-percentages finding - and separated by this one manipulation
span.quote: Memory-related activity in the parietal cortex differs from the memory trace held in frontal cortical neurons in that it is disrupted by intervening, distracting stimuli; the activity of parietal neurons represents the most recent stimulus to appear, whether it was behaviorally relevant or not ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 1996 ). In contrast, frontal neurons continue to discharge even after the presentation of intervening stimuli, representing the behaviorally relevant stimulus held in memory

span.label: working memory —same-as→ short-term memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — SAME REFERENT, different emphasis - the paper says outright that the newer term does not name a different system. Neither synonymy by fiat nor a renaming across fields: a reframing
span.quote: Working memory does not refer to a memory system that differs from that of short-term memory; the term rather emphasizes that this type of memory does not function simply as a passive storage of information but it allows integration of remembered information with current contingencies and future goals.

span.label: visual-spatial sketchpad —operationalised-as→ posterior parietal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak — OFFERED IN THE CONCLUSION AND HEDGED ('could provide'). The body of the same paper denies this mapping at the level of the region pair - see the mapping_declined limitation. Weight kept low deliberately
span.quote: Posterior parietal activity could provide a physiological correlate to the “visual-spatial sketchpad” in Allan Baddeley’s model of working memory by allowing for the manipulation of items held in working memory into larger organized structures.

span.label: visual-spatial sketchpad —part-of→ central executive
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — both are FUNCTIONAL units of a psychological model, which the paper warns are not anatomical
span.quote: Recent models propose four subsystems of working memory, a “central executive,” responsible for controlling and coordinating information through “slave” systems called the visual-spatial sketchpad for manipulation of visual objects, the phonological loop for verbal rehearsal, and the latest addition, an episodic buffer, that allows for temporal storage and binding of information within the other subsidiary subsystems

span.label: RETRACTED (NEITHER ENDPOINT IS ATTESTED AS WRITTEN) · area 7a —part-of→ posterior parietal cortex
span.note: RETRACTED: NEITHER ENDPOINT IS ATTESTED AS WRITTEN. The edge is `area 7a --part-of--> posterior parietal cortex`. The span: 'Virtually identical percentages of neurons exhibiting working memory responses were observed IN PARIETAL AREAS 7A AND LIP and prefrontal areas 46 and FEF.' The paper writes `parietal areas 7a and LIP`; the edge writes `area 7a` and `posterior parietal cortex`. THE CONTAINMENT IS TRUE OF THE FIELD - 7a is a posterior parietal area - AND THE SPAN NEVER SAYS IT, which is the commonest fault in this corpus and one this edge shares with the 66 expanded-endpoint rows measured this hour. Predates the Q-267 endpoint check and would be refused today. Found by the neighbour query (Q-400). Q-423. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The similarity in patterns of activity between prefrontal and parietal neurons was also confirmed by neurophysiological studies in both areas. Virtually identical percentages of neurons exhibiting working memory responses were observed in parietal areas 7a and LIP and prefrontal areas 46 and FEF

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · LIP —part-of→ posterior parietal cortex
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span compared prefrontal and parietal neurons without naming LIP's container. This sentence names both: working memory activity 'IN THE POSTERIOR PARIETAL CORTEX' described as 'discharges in monkey AREA LIP'. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The similarity in patterns of activity between prefrontal and parietal neurons was also confirmed by neurophysiological studies in both areas. Virtually identical percentages of neurons exhibiting working memory responses were observed in parietal areas 7a and LIP and prefrontal areas 46 and FEF

span.label: distracting stimuli —causes→ delay period
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — SIGN: destructive in parietal cortex, harmless in prefrontal - the asymmetry IS the demarcation
span.quote: Memory-related activity in the parietal cortex differs from the memory trace held in frontal cortical neurons in that it is disrupted by intervening, distracting stimuli; the activity of parietal neurons represents the most recent stimulus to appear, whether it was behaviorally relevant or not ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 1996 ). In contrast, frontal neurons continue to discharge even after the presentation of intervening stimuli, representing the behaviorally relevant stimulus held in memory

span.label: NMDA —causes→ attractor
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — a receptor time constant proposed as what makes the network state holdable at low firing rates
span.quote: A critical property revealed by models is that discharges can be sustained if the postsynaptic neuron continues to be in an excited state at the time presynaptic inputs accumulate. Given the fairly low firing rate of cortical pyramidal neurons, postsynaptic receptors with fairly slow time constants are essential for this function. The NMDA receptor has therefore been proposed as a critical element of cortical circuits involved in working memory

span.label: cortical cooling —operationalised-as→ prefrontal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — deactivating either region changes the other's output, which is how their interdependence was shown
span.quote: The importance in the interaction between the two areas was revealed by deactivation of either PPC or PFC by cortical cooling which was shown to produce a profound effect on the output of neurons in the other area

span.label: chunking —causes→ working memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — SIGN: increases effective capacity by restructuring the items rather than enlarging the store
span.quote: A strategy known as “chunking” ( Miller, 1956 ) takes small pieces of information and combines them into meaningful groups that constitute larger, single units of information. This type of manipulation is used in reading, language acquisition and many types of expert learning e.g. chess ( Gobet, Lane, Croker, Cheng, Jones, Oliver, & Pine, 2001 ). In humans, the use of structured grouping strategies in working memory can help reduce the working memory load and allow far greater amounts of information to be retained simultaneously

span.label: spectral power —operationalised-as→ selective attention
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — a decrease at 5-10 Hz distinguishes attending from remembering, in trained animals
span.quote: The results demonstrated that active attention and maintenance of a stimulus in working memory was characterized by distinct firing patterns, most notably a decrease in spectral power in the 5–10 Hz frequency range.

span.label: Brodmann —operationalised-as→ posterior parietal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — one of three schemes for saying where the region is, and the three do not agree across species
span.quote: The gross level differences in area placements between species are immediately obvious in the anatomical atlases. In the human, Brodmann’s areas 5 and 7 reside within the superior temporal lobule while areas 40 and 39 occupy most of the inferior parietal lobule. In monkeys, area 5 is found in the superior parietal lobule whereas areas 7a and 7b fall in the inferior parietal lobule. Brodmann’s Areas 39 and 40 have not been identified in the monkey.

span.label: LIP —part-of→ posterior parietal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS Rawley2009-neural-correlates-of-learning-and-working-me[5]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Initial reports of working memory activity in the posterior parietal cortex described discharges in monkey area LIP that followed the offset of a visual stimulus which was to be a target for a planned eye movement ( Gnadt & Andersen, 1988 ).

span.label: Parietal delay activity is overwritten by intervening distractors and codes whichever stimulus appeared most recently, while prefrontal neurons keep coding the behaviourally relevant one.
span.quote: Memory-related activity in the parietal cortex differs from the memory trace held in frontal cortical neurons in that it is disrupted by intervening, distracting stimuli; the activity of parietal neurons represents the most recent stimulus to appear, whether it was behaviorally relevant or not ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 1996 ).

span.label: The proportion of neurons showing working-memory activity is essentially the same in parietal areas 7a and LIP as in prefrontal areas 46 and FEF.
span.quote: Virtually identical percentages of neurons exhibiting working memory responses were observed in parietal areas 7a and LIP and prefrontal areas 46 and FEF ( Chafee & Goldman-Rakic, 1998 ).

span.label: Area 7a neurons hold the remembered location of a visual stimulus even when no motor response to it is planned, so the signal is mnemonic rather than motor-preparatory.
span.quote: Later studies in area 7a demonstrated that posterior parietal neurons represent the remembered locations of visual stimuli, independent of a planned motor response ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 1996 ).

span.label: Learning leaves a spectral signature in parietal spike trains: attending to and holding a stimulus in working memory lowers spectral power in the 5-10 Hz band.
span.quote: The results demonstrated that active attention and maintenance of a stimulus in working memory was characterized by distinct firing patterns, most notably a decrease in spectral power in the 5–10 Hz frequency range.

span.label: Colour selectivity in posterior parietal neurons, normally low, increases once colour becomes the cue that signifies which eye movement to make.
span.quote: However when animals execute a behavioral task for which color is important because it signifies eye movements, a larger percentage of PPC neurons exhibit selectivity for the color of the stimuli ( Toth & Assad, 2002 ).

span.label: TMS during the delay period slows responses whether applied over prefrontal or parietal cortex, but TMS during the decision period impairs performance only over prefrontal cortex.
span.quote: Similarly, right Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) applied over both prefrontal and posterior parietal cortex during the delay phase of a spatial working memory task increased reaction times whereas TMS applied during the decision phase of the task disrupted performance only when applied over the prefrontal, but not PPC ( Koch, Oliveri, Torriero, Carlesimo, Turriziani, & Caltagirone, 2005 ).

span.label: Monkeys trained on a salience-detection task signal the target faster and with more discriminable activity than untrained monkeys, although the overall response pattern is unchanged.
span.quote: These studies revealed that although the overall pattern of responses was similar, neuronal activity in monkeys trained to detect a salient stimulus in a visual display reflected the target faster, and produced a more discriminable level of activation.

span.label: Imaging meta-analysis places area 7 in every executive component of working memory tested - ordering, updating and manipulating items - as well as in spatial content.
span.quote: A meta-analysis of imaging studies involving working memory tasks revealed that area 7 was reliably activated by all aspects of executive function examined (ordering, updating, and manipulating items held in working memory), as well as the spatial content of working memory ( Wager & Smith, 2003 ).

span.label: parietal and prefrontal cortex show virtually identical proportions of neurons with working memory responses
span.quote: The similarity in patterns of activity between prefrontal and parietal neurons was also confirmed by neurophysiological studies in both areas. Virtually identical percentages of neurons exhibiting working memory responses were observed in parietal areas 7a and LIP and prefrontal areas 46 and FEF

span.label: parietal delay activity is overwritten by an intervening distractor; prefrontal activity is not
span.quote: Memory-related activity in the parietal cortex differs from the memory trace held in frontal cortical neurons in that it is disrupted by intervening, distracting stimuli; the activity of parietal neurons represents the most recent stimulus to appear, whether it was behaviorally relevant or not ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 1996 ). In contrast, frontal neurons continue to discharge even after the presentation of intervening stimuli, representing the behaviorally relevant stimulus held in memory

span.label: TMS over prefrontal cortex disrupted the decision phase of a memory task while TMS over parietal cortex did not
span.quote: Similarly, right Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) applied over both prefrontal and posterior parietal cortex during the delay phase of a spatial working memory task increased reaction times whereas TMS applied during the decision phase of the task disrupted performance only when applied over the prefrontal, but not PPC

span.label: cooling either region changes the output of the other, so the two are not independent modules
span.quote: The importance in the interaction between the two areas was revealed by deactivation of either PPC or PFC by cortical cooling which was shown to produce a profound effect on the output of neurons in the other area

span.label: parietal neurons acquire colour selectivity when colour becomes task-relevant, having had little before
span.quote: PPC neurons typically have low selectivity for color; only a small percentage of area 7a neurons demonstrate significantly different responses to green and red stimuli of equal luminance ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 2001 ). However when animals execute a behavioral task for which color is important because it signifies eye movements, a larger percentage of PPC neurons exhibit selectivity for the color of the stimuli

span.label: trained animals' parietal neurons signalled the target faster and more discriminably than naive animals'
span.quote: A more fundamental effect of learning was revealed by comparing responses of PPC neurons in animals trained to perform a behavioral task ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 2001 ) with responses in animals naïve to behavioral training ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 2005 ). These studies revealed that although the overall pattern of responses was similar, neuronal activity in monkeys trained to detect a salient stimulus in a visual display reflected the target faster, and produced a more discriminable level of activation.

span.label: attention and memory maintenance are separable by a fall in 5-10 Hz spectral power
span.quote: The results demonstrated that active attention and maintenance of a stimulus in working memory was characterized by distinct firing patterns, most notably a decrease in spectral power in the 5–10 Hz frequency range.

span.label: two patients with frontal lesions and no neglect still failed spatial working memory, dissociating the two deficits
span.quote: Interestingly, poor performance was also observed in two patients with right lateral frontal lesions who showed no neglect ( Malhotra, 2005 ), confirming that a dissociation can exist between spatial working memory and neglect in some cases.

span.label: the Corsi task was modified to put all items on the vertical midline, removing the attentional bias from the memory measure
span.quote: In the latter study, modified versions of the Corsi blocks task were used to dissociate the working memory aspect of the pathology from neglect; viewers had to remember the order of a series of highlighted discs whose locations were restricted to the vertical midline, thus eliminating the attentional bias towards the ipsilesional visual field.

span.label: MAPPING DECLINED: the parietal-prefrontal specialisation does not correspond to Baddeley's subsystems, since both regions do visual-spatial and executive work
span.quote: It should be noted however that this specialization does not correspond to distinct components or subsystems of the Baddeley model, as both visual-spatial and executive functions have been described in both parietal and prefrontal areas.

span.label: MAPPING OFFERED, HEDGED: the conclusion nonetheless proposes parietal activity as a possible correlate of the visual-spatial sketchpad
span.quote: Posterior parietal activity could provide a physiological correlate to the “visual-spatial sketchpad” in Allan Baddeley’s model of working memory by allowing for the manipulation of items held in working memory into larger organized structures.

span.label: four incompatible accounts of what sustained prefrontal activity represents are listed without adjudication
span.quote: Contrary to the buffer concept, Miller and Cohen propose that activity sustained in PFC may represent a goal along with an associated plan of action, rather than a memory trace for a particular item ( Miller & Cohen, 2001 ). It has also been posited that instead of being maintained in dedicated modality-specific buffers, information held in working memory is represented by the activity of those processes within the current focus of attention ( Cowan, 1988 ). Along similar lines, the idea has evolved that working memory is an emergent property of cognition and the network of rain regions that mediate it

span.label: working memory
span.quote: Closely tied with the function of selective attention is working memory, or the ability to keep pieces of pertinent information temporarily available during ongoing execution of a mental operation.

span.label: chunking
span.quote: A strategy known as “chunking” ( Miller, 1956 ) takes small pieces of information and combines them into meaningful groups that constitute larger, single units of information.

span.label: set shifting
span.quote: Behavior involving rule updating under changing task demands is known as set shifting and one of the most striking deficits observed is in patients suffering from frontal lobe lesions is the inability to do this successfully.

span.label: Balint's syndrome
span.quote: The most severe effects of bilateral parietal lesions produce Balint’s syndrome, characterized by the inability to perceive more than one visual stimulus at a time, to direct visual attention outside the fovea, to scan visual space, and to coordinate hand movements to visual targets ( Constantinidis, 2006b ).

span.label: memory simultanagnosia
span.quote: A related possibility is that this disruption in internal attention is caused by “memory simultanagnosia”, an inability to pay attention to more than one memory at once ( Cabeza, 2008 ; Cabeza et al., 2008 ).

span.label: the four functional domains of posterior parietal cortex
span.term: the four functional domains of posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: Functions of the PPC can be grouped in four domains: sensorimotor transformations, selective attention, working memory, and learning.

span.label: selective attention
span.quote: A second important function of the posterior parietal cortex is to act as a mediator of this process, known as selective attention.

span.label: working memory
span.quote: Closely tied with the function of selective attention is working memory, or the ability to keep pieces of pertinent information temporarily available during ongoing execution of a mental operation.

span.label: short-term memory
span.quote: Working memory does not refer to a memory system that differs from that of short-term memory; the term rather emphasizes that this type of memory does not function simply as a passive storage of information but it allows integration of remembered information with current contingencies and future goals.

span.label: chunking
span.quote: A strategy known as “chunking” ( Miller, 1956 ) takes small pieces of information and combines them into meaningful groups that constitute larger, single units of information. This type of manipulation is used in reading, language acquisition and many types of expert learning e.g. chess ( Gobet, Lane, Croker, Cheng, Jones, Oliver, & Pine, 2001 ). In humans, the use of structured grouping strategies in working memory can help reduce the working memory load and allow far greater amounts of information to be retained simultaneously

span.label: set shifting
span.quote: Behavior involving rule updating under changing task demands is known as set shifting and one of the most striking deficits observed is in patients suffering from frontal lobe lesions is the inability to do this successfully. Human studies indicate that set shifting involves posterior parietal regions as well

span.label: neglect
span.quote: Perhaps the signature effect of PPC damage is the neglect syndrome, typically occurring after a lesion in the right hemisphere. Disturbances include the inability to detect an object in the contralateral (left) visual hemifield (egocentric neglect) or to perceive the left side of objects, regardless of where they appear within the visual field (allocentric neglect).

span.label: attractor
span.quote: Reverberatory networks, when left unperturbed, will settle into an attractor state defined by a stereotyped pattern of activity within the network ( Hopfield, 1982 ). Attractor models may undergo spontaneous oscillations, although network instantiations have also been shown to be capable of mediating sustained responses without oscillatory discharges

span.label: 5 cm — the distance from the face within which "ultranear" VIP neurons encode a visual stimulus
span.quote: Another distinguishing feature of VIP is sensitivity for the distance of stimuli, with “ultranear” neurons encoding visual stimuli only when they come within 5 cm of the face ( Colby et al., 1993 ).

span.label: 5–10 Hz — the frequency band in which spectral power of parietal spike trains drops during attention and working-memory maintenance after training
span.quote: The results demonstrated that active attention and maintenance of a stimulus in working memory was characterized by distinct firing patterns, most notably a decrease in spectral power in the 5–10 Hz frequency range.

span.label: 5-10 Hz — the band whose power falls during attention and memory maintenance after training
span.quote: The results demonstrated that active attention and maintenance of a stimulus in working memory was characterized by distinct firing patterns, most notably a decrease in spectral power in the 5–10 Hz frequency range.

span.label: areas 5, 7, 40 and 39 — the human Brodmann areas making up posterior parietal cortex, two of which have no monkey counterpart
span.quote: The gross level differences in area placements between species are immediately obvious in the anatomical atlases. In the human, Brodmann’s areas 5 and 7 reside within the superior temporal lobule while areas 40 and 39 occupy most of the inferior parietal lobule. In monkeys, area 5 is found in the superior parietal lobule whereas areas 7a and 7b fall in the inferior parietal lobule. Brodmann’s Areas 39 and 40 have not been identified in the monkey.

span.label: four — subsystems in the current Baddeley model, all functional rather than anatomical
span.quote: Recent models propose four subsystems of working memory, a “central executive,” responsible for controlling and coordinating information through “slave” systems called the visual-spatial sketchpad for manipulation of visual objects, the phonological loop for verbal rehearsal, and the latest addition, an episodic buffer, that allows for temporal storage and binding of information within the other subsidiary subsystems

span.label: meta-analysis
span.quote: It should be noted however that this specialization does not correspond to distinct components or subsystems of the Baddeley model, as both visual-spatial and executive functions have been described in both parietal and prefrontal areas.

span.label: distracting stimuli
span.quote: Memory-related activity in the parietal cortex differs from the memory trace held in frontal cortical neurons in that it is disrupted by intervening, distracting stimuli; the activity of parietal neurons represents the most recent stimulus to appear, whether it was behaviorally relevant or not ( Constantinidis & Steinmetz, 1996 ). In contrast, frontal neurons continue to discharge even after the presentation of intervening stimuli, representing the behaviorally relevant stimulus held in memory
